2608.13263.title: vToken: Token-Level Virtualization for Reclaimable KV Caches
2608.13263.paper_summary: Large language model serving faces a critical memory bottleneck: the KV cache grows with sequence length and batch size. PagedAttention uses fixed-size memory blocks to reduce allocator-level fragmentation, but recent KV eviction algorithms operate at a token granularity finer than block-level management. This mismatch causes intra-block fragmentation, leaving a large fraction of allocated KV memory unreclaimable. We present vToken, a lightweight token-level virtualization layer that decouples logical token liveness from physical block placement. vToken maintains a stable logical token view through token-table indirection and realizes physical reclamation by repacking live tokens asynchronously. The design preserves PagedAttention kernels and CUDA Graph compatibility. We implement vToken in vLLM and evaluate it with H2O, Random, and Scissorhands across models. Compared with a paired Naive-Evict baseline, vToken reduces retained KV blocks per request by 27.2\%--72.3\% and improves SLA-constrained throughput by up to 1.37$\times$. Under a constrained active-KV budget, it extends the maximum feasible concurrency by up to 2$\times$, while reducing the per-policy integration footprint from 500+ lines to under 50.
2608.13263.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型面臨一個關鍵的記憶體瓶頸：KV 快取隨著序列長度和批次大小的增長而增長。PagedAttention 使用固定大小的記憶體區塊來減少分配器層級的碎片化，但最近的 KV 驅逐算法在比區塊層級管理更細的標記粒度上運作。這種不匹配導致區塊內部碎片化，使得大量分配的 KV 記憶體無法回收。我們提出了 vToken，一個輕量級的標記級虛擬化層，將邏輯標記的存活性與物理區塊的放置解耦。vToken 通過標記表間接保持穩定的邏輯標記視圖，並通過異步重新打包活躍標記來實現物理回收。該設計保留了 PagedAttention 核心和 CUDA Graph 的兼容性。我們在 vLLM 中實現了 vToken，並在模型上使用 H2O、Random 和 Scissorhands 進行評估。與配對的 Naive-Evict 基準相比，vToken 每個請求減少了 27.2\%--72.3\% 的保留 KV 區塊，並將 SLA 約束的吞吐量提高了最多 1.37$\times$。在受限的活躍-KV 預算下，它將最大可行的並發性擴展了最多 2$\times$，同時將每個策略的整合代碼量從 500 多行減少到 50 行以下。
